proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched shrinking-radius causal risk and honest-interval frontier with an exact-law packing, a total finite estimator, and a fixed-class Gaussian covariance lower bound. The D0.5 math panel passed and six cited facts were verified, but the general referee capped the delivered package at subfield because of its narrow calibrated model and impractical estimator. D0.5 stopped at triage; theorem-positioning and ballast findings remain unrepaired, and no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The constant causal slope has all-estimator minimax squared risk \(r_{n,a}=n^{-1}+a^2\rho(na^2)^2\) throughout every fixed public window \(na^8\le\kappa<\infty\). A total finite positive-moment estimator attains this rate on the original Gaussian--Rademacher records, and its uniformly honest \(90\%\) connected interval has minimax expected length of order \(\sqrt{r_{n,a}}\). The resolved canonical Hermite-transfer theorem supplies the legal weighted comparisons. A fixed-radius reflected pair also proves risk lower order \(\rho(n)^2\) and honest connected-interval length lower order \(\rho(n)\) for the identifiable Gaussian-component covariance coordinate on the published bivariate Gaussian mixture-class specialization.
gap: Published Gaussian-mixture inverse results establish the fixed-radius logarithmic exponent, while existing causal results separate exact Gaussian noise from fixed non-Gaussian cumulants. None tracks the shrinking treatment-coordinate radius, the resulting effective size \(na^2\), and honest inference in the original Gaussian--Rademacher records for every fixed finite \(\kappa\).
fill: The project evaluates the positive compact bivariate slope modulus, constructs a terminating data-only moment-fit with a fourth-moment certificate, and converts a direct exact-law packing into same-class minimax risk and connected-interval length bounds.
